integration_notes: Upstream ships 3D GPUParticles3D particle scenes and a C# helper (scripts/MultiParticles.cs). This project is Godot 4.7 GDScript-only 2D (BC-02), so the two effects actually used (shockwave, sparks) were adapted to 2D CPUParticles2D scenes under particles/ instead of copying the 3D originals (sanctioned by the goal-card constraint '3D 粒子按 BC-01 适配'). Texture references keep the upstream res://addons/kenney_particle_pack/ paths.
Source textures are 512x512, so the 2D scenes restate upstream curve/ramp/velocity values in 2D pixel terms (upstream scale/velocity values assume small 3D units).

camera-effects scenes are full-rect ColorRect + ShaderMaterial pairs used as-is (byte-identical). scripts/main.gd instantiates them at runtime into the Background CanvasLayer (layer -1) of scenes/main.tscn, i.e. below the board canvas, so no effect node can obscure the board, pieces or HUD data (BC-06). Visibility envelopes (<= 0.5 s, fixed strength, no settings) are driven by scripts/main.gd _tick_fx.

chromatic_aberration.tscn defaults focus_radius=0/focus_edge=0 make smoothstep(edge0==edge1) input undefined on some GPUs; scripts/main.gd sets shader_parameter/focus_edge=0.001 at runtime for a deterministic full-strength result. The vendored scene file itself is not modified.
Upstream camera-effect scenes leave ColorRect.mouse_filter at the default STOP; scripts/main.gd sets MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE on the runtime instances (no vendored file modified).
Upstream .import files were not copied: import metadata is regenerated by this project's Godot 4.7.2 headless editor import (importer versions/uids differ per project).

The C# MultiParticles.cs simultaneity behavior is replaced by scripts/main.gd restarting the one-shot node.
